legal_basis.title: Intra-EU VAT number confirmation
legal_basis.ref: Council Directive 2006/112/EC, art. 138(1)(b); Council Regulation (EU) No 904/2010, art. 31
legal_basis.summary: The VAT exemption for intra-EU supplies requires the customer to hold a valid VAT identification number in another member state; member states must let businesses confirm a number's validity electronically (VIES).

legal_basis.title: EU AML customer due diligence
legal_basis.ref: Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD4/5), art. 13(1)(a); Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR, applicable from 10 July 2027), art. 20 and 22
legal_basis.summary: Obliged entities must identify the customer and verify identity on the basis of documents, data or information from a reliable and independent source. Official registries such as VIES are such a source for the existence of a VAT-registered business; they are not sufficient on their own for beneficial-ownership checks.

legal_basis.title: Verification of Payee (payee name vs IBAN)
legal_basis.ref: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 (Instant Payments Regulation), art. 5c of Regulation (EU) 260/2012
legal_basis.summary: Since 9 October 2025, EU payment providers must check that the payee name matches the IBAN before a credit transfer. This tool's name and IBAN checks are an upstream, registry-based complement, not a bank VoP response.

legal_basis.title: Data minimisation
legal_basis.summary: The report masks the IBAN and only a SHA-256 digest of it enters the attestation. Nothing is stored server-side; nothing personal is written on-chain.

legal_basis.title: No solely automated decision with legal effect
legal_basis.summary: Where counterparties are natural persons (e.g. sole traders), a decision with legal or similarly significant effect must not rest solely on automated processing: the report always carries a human-review flag and note.

legal_basis.title: Lawful basis for the checks
legal_basis.ref: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), art. 6(1)(c) legal obligation (AML) and 6(1)(f) legitimate interest (fraud prevention, recital 47)
legal_basis.summary: Checking a business counterparty against public registries before paying it is covered by a legal obligation for obliged entities and by the legitimate interest in preventing fraud for others.
